title: Practice interview: junior data engineer
intro: Type each turn as you would say it. Typing stands in for speech in this prototype.
You can ask what a term means, or ask me to repeat a question. My replies come from a prepared sheet, the same for every candidate, so I can't give hints.
After each turn I show how I read it: your answer, a question, or still thinking. If I read it wrong, one tap fixes it.
I can misread a turn. When I'm not sure, I ask you.
I don't score anything. A person reads the record, and you see it at the end.

phrases.ask: Was that your answer, or a question for me?
phrases.ask_no_model: I couldn't read that turn. Was it your answer, or a question for me?
phrases.stuck: No rush. Do you want to keep thinking, hear the question again, or move on?
phrases.decline: I can't help with that one. I can only give the clarifications prepared for this question, the same for every candidate. Answer it as you see it.
phrases.back: Sorry, I took that as your answer. Going back to question {n}.
phrases.moved_on: Moving on. No answer is recorded for that question.
phrases.end: That was the last question. Below is the record a person will read. I have not scored anything.

common.when: asks to hear, see or repeat the question again
asks whether they may answer with a different tool, language or system than the one named
common.say: Yes. Use the tools you know, and say which ones.

common.when: asks how long or how detailed the answer should be
common.say: A few sentences are enough: the main idea, then one detail.

common.when: asks for a moment to think
asks whether their own idea, approach or answer is right, or asks for a hint
common.say: I can't say whether an approach is right, and I can't give hints. A person judges the answers. Tell me what you would do, and why.

questions.ask: How would you make a dbt model incremental, so that it only processes new rows?

sheet.when: asks what dbt is, or whether the question is about dbt, or says they have not used dbt
sheet.say: dbt is a tool that builds warehouse tables from SQL files called models. If you haven't used it, describe how you would do the same with a tool you know.
Incremental means each run handles only new or changed rows, not the whole table.

sheet.when: asks what a model is in dbt
sheet.say: A dbt model is one SQL query saved as a file. dbt builds a table or a view from it.

questions.ask: What is a slowly changing dimension, and how would you keep its history?

sheet.when: asks what a dimension is, or what dimension means here
sheet.say: A dimension is a table that describes things in a data warehouse, such as customers or products.

sheet.when: asks whether a particular type is meant, such as type 1 or type 2
sheet.say: Any type is fine. Say which one you are describing.

questions.ask: What is the difference between a star schema and a snowflake schema?

sheet.say: Here a schema is the way the tables in a data warehouse are laid out and joined.

sheet.when: asks whether to define, compare or give examples
sheet.say: Say how the two differ, and when you would choose each.

questions.ask: Events sometimes arrive twice from a stream. How would you remove the duplicates?

sheet.when: asks whether a duplicate event is an exact copy of the original
sheet.say: Yes. Assume a duplicate is an exact copy of the original event.

sheet.when: asks whether this is during streaming or after the data is loaded
sheet.say: Either is fine. Say which one you are describing.

sheet.when: asks which system, warehouse or streaming tool is used
sheet.say: No particular system. Use one you know.

questions.ask: A daily pipeline failed overnight. What do you check first, and why?

sheet.when: asks what the pipeline does, or which tool runs it
sheet.say: Assume a daily batch job that loads files into a warehouse, run by a scheduler such as Airflow.

sheet.when: asks what logs, alerts or monitoring are available
sheet.say: Assume you have the scheduler's logs and nothing else.

sheet.when: asks whether to fix the problem or only find the cause
sheet.say: Say what you would look at first and why. A full fix is not needed.
